title: Training-session tampered-credential test always changes the signature

problem_register.description: Required check that fails without load: test_live_tampered_credential_rejected_by_owner replaced the last base64url character of a 43-char HS256 signature ('A' -> 'B'), which modifies only the 2 trailing base64 padding bits (~1/16 runs when exp=time.time() produces a signature ending in 'A') and decodes to identical signature bytes.

runtime_budget.details: Test-only change in services/control-plane/bff/test_training_session_service_client.py. No production code, recurring job, emitter, or persistent writer is added or modified.

fix_summary.mechanism: Splits the signed JWT into header_b64, payload_b64, and sig_b64; base64url-decodes sig_b64 into orig_sig_bytes; flips bit 0 of byte 0 (tampered_sig_raw[0] ^= 0x01); canonically base64url-encodes the modified bytes without '=' padding; asserts decoded_tampered_sig != orig_sig_bytes before calling ports.create_trainer_session; and asserts the owner rejects the tampered credential with HTTP 401.

loop_200_fresh_token_verification.command:
.venv-pantheon/bin/python3 -c 'import sys, pytest; tokens = []; class Repeat200:
    def pytest_collection_modifyitems(self, session, config, items):
        mod = items[0].module; orig_jwt = mod._signed_caller_jwt
        def wrapped_jwt(*a, **kw):
            tok = orig_jwt(*a, **kw); tokens.append(tok); return tok
        mod._signed_caller_jwt = wrapped_jwt
        items[:] = [pytest.Function.from_parent(item.parent, name=f"{item.name}[{i}]", callobj=item.obj) for item in items for i in range(200)]
rc = pytest.main(["-q", "services/control-plane/bff/test_training_session_service_client.py::test_live_tampered_credential_rejected_by_owner"], plugins=[Repeat200()]); ending_in_a = sum(1 for t in tokens if t.endswith("A")); print(f"runs={len(tokens)} unique_tokens={len(set(tokens))} ending_in_A={ending_in_a} rc={rc}"); assert rc == 0 and len(tokens) == 200 and len(set(tokens)) == 200'

matches_examined.disposition: Fixed in this change by flipping a bit of the decoded signature bytes and re-encoding canonically.

Not a defect: inside test_corrupt_sig_helper_adversarial_cases(), this intentionally constructs a trailing-padding-bit variant to verify that _corrupt_sig(sig) (which flips raw[0] ^= 0xFF on decoded bytes) still produces distinct decoded signature bytes.
